About the University

We have one simple promise – to make a positive impact. Through our ground-breaking research, teaching excellence and commitment to sustainable living, we are changing lives for the better.

The University of Derby is a modern university with a modern outlook. Everything we do is driven by delivering excellence and opportunities for our students, our staff and our region.

We have some of the best university facilities in the UK and achieve outstanding results for our teaching and research and have been awarded Gold in the prestigious Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) 2023 – making it one of the top universities in the country recognised for its outstanding student experience and student outcomes.

Financially strong and seriously ambitious we offer our employees an inclusive culture that centres itself around staff wellbeing, where you can be confident you will receive all the help and encouragement you need to build a rewarding career with lots of opportunities to enhance your skills.

About the College/Department

Here at the University of Derby, the College of Science and Engineering is the home STEM, the skills that are essential to the UK’s Industrial Strategy. From digitisation to decarbonisation, we have an important role to play in shaping the future. And by researching or collaborating with us, you can too.

The College brings together a powerful combination of scientific expertise, technological innovation, and creative practice. With disciplines spanning computing, AI, Data Science, engineering, environmental sciences, built environments and Psychology. We are uniquely positioned to solve real-world challenges through interdisciplinary collaboration.

Our courses are designed with employability and future industry needs in mind, supported by cutting-edge facilities, strong employer partnerships, and a commitment to sustainability. Through applied research and hands-on learning, we equip students and staff to drive progress in areas that matter most; from smart technology to clean energy, advanced manufacturing to immersive design.

School of Computing

This is an exciting time in Computing, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science at the University of Derby. Building on recent Research Excellence Framework (REF) success, our school has ambitions to become leaders in these areas. In the last ten years, we’ve invested heavily in our facilities, including a £13m STEM centre. We aspire to be at the forefront of teaching and research around topics such as machine learning, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and complex networks. The Collaborative and Data-Centric Engineering Research Cluster, part of the Data Science Research Centre, will play a key role in this project.

Our engagement with global industries based in the Derby region, for example through our East Midlands Institute of Technology, helps ensure that our research and teaching are at the forefront of emerging industry needs and opportunities. Our links with companies in our region including, Bloc Digital, Rolls-Royce and Alstom, also mean our students benefit from placement years and live briefs. 

About Sperry Rail (International) Ltd 

Sperry Rail is on a mission critical journey to revolutionize the Rail Flaw Detection industry. Through the continuous development of cutting-edge diagnostic technologies and AI assisted analysis, we are transforming railway safety worldwide. Our global engineering teams work collaboratively to develop step-change technologies that define Sperry as the unparalleled market leader. For nearly a century we have repeatedly succeeded in modernizing and improving rail diagnostics through our unrelenting pursuit of improvement. Determined is an understatement. We are obsessed with advancing the science and raising the bar on what’s possible with our ever improving suite of product and service offerings. Emboldened through the shared values of honesty, accountability, passion, integrity and teamwork, we are driven by the challenge and bridging concept with fruition. Each technologist entering Sperry has an opportunity to imprint themselves into our brand and further galvanize a culture of innovation and advancement. Allow us to be clear, Thought Leaders are welcome! We are agile, hungry and invite those with similar passion to join us in challenging the status quo and bringing new ideas to market. Fast paced, high-touch with distinct sense of purpose, we offer more than a job, rather an opportunity to be part of a something different.

About the role

University of Derby’s College of Science & Engineering in partnership with Sperry Rail (International) Limited are offering an exciting career-development opportunity to manage and deliver a challenging strategic Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) project. Based at Sperry Rail’s premises in Derby, you will be employed by the University as a KTP Associate but work under the terms and conditions of the company.

You will be responsible for developing an innovative and advanced method for the accurate localisation of rail defects through the integration of AI foundation models, digital twin technologies, GIS data, and multimodal data fusion. The project will involve investigating and prototyping state-of-the-art AI techniques to combine GPS signals, proximity imagery, railway infrastructure data, and inspection outputs for improved track-level positioning accuracy and automated defect localisation across complex railway networks. The KTP Associate will benefit from the support of a team of experts in the fields of artificial intelligence, digital twins, geospatial analytics, multimodal data fusion, and railway inspection technologies to develop and prototype the solutions.

You will be part of a 12 person team based in Derby. The Derby office will be available for the Associate to work with other team members who work a mix of office based and distance working. You will be expected to be present in the office for a minimum of three days a week and participate in daily stand-up meetings. You will also be interfacing with Sperry teams of AWS specialist sub-contractors and user interface software sub-contractors, and other related teams (e.g. non-destructive analysis, data acquisition, embedded systems, and possibly customer facing teams such as business development).

Using your knowledge and skills to support the business and achieve specific project aims, you will receive on-going support from a Sperry Rail Supervisor, Academic Supervisor and Academic Lead from the University of Derby to help you deliver. A personal training and development budget will also be available for you to access, as well as receiving access to the same training opportunities and facilities as University staff.

This is a dynamic role that presents an opportunity for an ambitious candidate to play an influential role in developing innovative AI-driven solutions for rail defect localisation, leveraging foundation models, digital twins, GIS technologies, and multimodal data fusion. This structured development project will involve investigating and prototyping cutting-edge techniques to improve track-level positioning accuracy and automated defect localisation across complex railway networks, while working across a range of departments to understand and solve complex business and technical challenges.

Knowledge Transfer Partnerships 

This full-time post is part-funded by the UK Government’s KTP programme. A KTP is a three-way project between a graduate, an organisation and a university. KTP is one of the UK’s largest graduate recruitment programmes and has been placing graduates on challenging, high profile projects for 50 years. In addition to a competitive salary and core KTP development training, you will have a dedicated budget of £5,000 further training and career development. To find out more about the scheme visit: ktp-uk.org/graduates 

Please note by completing an application form for this role, you are giving your consent for us to share your personal data with the KTP partner.

Please note that this vacancy will consist of a two-stage interview process. Shortlisted candidates should be available for:

Stage 1: Wednesday 16th December
Stage 2: Thursday 17th December

We encourage candidates to reserve both dates, as alternative interview dates will not be available.

About You

We’re looking for a talented and ambitious individual with experience developing AI-driven solutions that deliver real-world impact in complex operational environments. In this role, you’ll work on creating innovative rail defect localisation systems by combining AI foundation models, digital twins, GIS technologies, and multimodal data from sources such as GPS, railway inspection data, proximity imagery, and infrastructure records to improve positioning accuracy and support intelligent decision-making across railway networks.

You’ll bring strong experience in machine learning, deep learning, and Python software development, with the ability to design, build, and optimise scalable data processing and localisation pipelines. Experience working with multimodal data, geospatial information, computer vision, signal processing, or digital twin technologies will be highly valued. You’ll also have hands-on experience developing and prototyping advanced AI solutions, integrating data from multiple sources, and validating systems in real-world environments.

You will work both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams spanning academia and industry, bringing a proactive, innovative, and solutions-focused mindset. Strong communication skills are essential, with the ability to present complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, contribute to project dissemination activities, and engage effectively with colleagues, customers, and industry partners in the UK and internationally. 

Principal accountabilities
To lead the development of the KTP project, including: Designing and developing a novel AI foundation model that combines GPS data, proximity imagery, GIS information, and railway inspection data to deliver robust and accurate rail defect localisation across complex railway networks; Developing, testing, and integrating AI-enabled digital twin technologies and advanced data fusion approaches to support railway condition monitoring, intelligent visualisation, automated localisation, and enhanced decision-making for rail asset management; Building a topology-aware graph representation of the railway network and a localisation-centred digital twin platform, integrated with Sperry Rail's existing service platform.
To work with the academic team to disseminate the outcomes and research developed as part of the project.
To work with Sperry Rail and the academic team to integrate the developed system into a business platform and demonstrate its capabilities to key stakeholders in support of the company's future plans.
To prepare and present demonstration scenarios using real inspection data to Sperry Rail stakeholders and customers.
To provide training to the Sperry Rail R&D team on the use of the system and to deliver the technical documentation, project handover, and Innovate UK final report.
To carry out all work in a professional manner and engage in tasks and training as required by Sperry Rail, the University of Derby, and Innovate UK.

 The opportunity  

 You will play a key technical role in the development of machine learning and Edge AI technologies for wearable sensing systems in human-centred industrial applications. The role focuses on developing efficient and robust deep learning models for real-time surface electromyography (sEMG) signal processing, hand gesture recognition and prediction, and adaptive human–machine interfaces to improve worker safety, wellbeing, and productivity in real manufacturing environments.

 About you 

 We are seeking a self-motivated researcher with strong expertise in machine learning, deep learning, and Edge AI, particularly for real-time signal processing and resource-constrained embedded systems. The successful candidate will be expected to take technical ownership of an AI-focused research workstream, from model design and development through to optimisation, deployment, validation, and delivery.

 You will lead technical contributions to machine learning and Edge AI research and development, including the design, training, optimisation, and deployment of deep learning models on resource-constrained embedded platforms such as microcontrollers, embedded GPUs, and FPGAs. A key focus will be on achieving accurate, low-latency, and energy-efficient inference through advanced model optimisation techniques. You will also contribute to multimodal sensor fusion, model adaptation across users and operating conditions, and the integration and validation of AI solutions within wearable sensing systems for real-world industrial deployment.

 You will have;  

 A PhD (or near completion, or equivalent industrial research experience) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a closely related discipline.

 Demonstrated experience in Edge AI and efficient deep learning, including model optimisation, compression, and deployment on resource-constrained.

 Strong programming skills in Python/C/C++ and deep learning frameworks.

 A strong research track record in leading related conferences and journals (e.g. NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICRA, IROS, or equivalent venues).

 A demonstrated ability to independently deliver technical research milestones within collaborative projects, supported by strong organisational skills and effective time management.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, creativity in addressing technical challenges, and the ability to collaborate effectively with academic and industrial partners. 

 The role will be based at School of Computer Science and Informatics and the School of Engineering, working closely with Dr. Baoru Huang (School of Computer Science and Informatics), Dr. Simon Maher (Department of Electrical Engineering & Electronics), and Dr. Anh Nguyen (School of Computer Science and Informatics), alongside our European partners.

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

The Health Economics and Decision Science (HEDS) section within the School of Medicine & Population Health is seeking to appoint a Grade 7 Research Associate in Public Health Economic Modelling. The role will contribute to an applied research project focused on symptomatic lung cancer detection in primary care, with particular emphasis on individual-level decision model simulation and health economic evaluation. You will join a multidisciplinary team undertaking applied research to inform public health policy and decision making.

 

As part of the team, you will contribute to applied research on novel cancer detection interventions, with a particular focus on developing and applying individual level decision model simulations. You will work with data and evidence to parameterise, test and validate models; assess uncertainty; interpret findings; and contribute to technical reports and peer reviewed publications. Working with guidance from senior colleagues, you will take responsibility for agreed areas of modelling and analysis and contribute to wider HEDS activities.

 

Candidates should possess at least a Master's level qualification in health economics, together with relevant work experience in health economics, economic evaluation or decision modelling. You should have strong quantitative skills and practical experience of decision analytic modelling, ideally including individual level modelling, and be able to use appropriate software such as R, Python, VBA or advanced Excel. PhD level research experience is essential. Experience of modelling screening interventions would be an advantage.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Undertake applied research in health economics, under the guidance of senior colleagues, taking responsibility for agreed components of individual level decision model simulation and the health economic evaluation of blood biomarkers for lung cancer detection within the primary care symptomatic pathway 
Develop, implement, test, validate and document the individual level decision model simulation using appropriate software, ensuring that model structure, assumptions, logic and code are transparent, reproducible and appropriately quality assured.
Undertake statistical and data analysis and prepare model inputs using project datasets and other relevant evidence, with appropriate data checking and documentation.
Contribute to activities (e.g. literature review, evidence synthesis and elicitation activities) to identify, estimate and justify model parameters, and undertake appropriate sensitivity, scenario and uncertainty analyses.
Interpret and communicate model results, assumptions, limitations and uncertainty clearly to research collaborators, policy and practice stakeholders, and other relevant audiences.
Prepare high quality research outputs, including technical model documentation, research reports, project updates, conference presentations and manuscripts for peer reviewed publication.
Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary research partners and collaborators within and outside the University, contribute actively to project meetings, and support the timely delivery of agreed research objectives.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. The combined university is now one of the largest higher education destinations for London students, combining a breadth of disciplines across health, business, policy, law, creativity, communications, science and technology. Our students are at the heart of everything that we do, and we are committed to supporting them to pursue their career and personal ambitions.

 Our research is engaged, at the frontier of practice and has a positive impact on the world around us.

 Background 

 CSGUoL and Mosdorfer Rail Ltd (Mosdorfer) are recruiting for a candidate to develop a novel non-contact tri-electrode field mill voltage detector that can detect voltages in overhead catenary lines or third rail systems simultaneously. 

 Mosdorfer Rail Ltd operates in the UK as a specialist manufacturer and supplier of railway electrification components, with a focus on overhead line (catenary) systems for rail and tram networks. 

 Responsibilities 

 This KTP will address a market/technological gap through the design and development of a novel tri-electrode field mill voltage detector which can detect LVDC, MVDC and 25kV AC simultaneously. Core responsibilities include converting knowledge into usable, reusable engineering assets of Mosdorfer, including design, simulation, calibration and signal processing tools. The Associate will embed knowledge into standardised, repeatable workflows (SOPs), including design, build, calibration, field deployment and validation, supported by detailed documentation and training. 

 Person Specification 

 We are looking for a candidate with a BEng/MSc or other Higher Degree in Electrical and Electronic Engineering with a focus on High-Voltage or Power-Engineering. The Associate will have knowledge of high-voltage engineering, electromagnetic fields and safety standards, as well as experience in analogue circuit design. 

 The ideal candidate will have knowledge of power engineering and experience of insulation and electric field management, as well as prior experience working within the electrical/electronic engineering sector, and experience of embedded software development.

Research Assistant in Digitalisation of Bioenergy

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. 

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.  

The role

The successful candidate will work as an integral part of the new Supergen Bioenergy Impact Hub, supporting the Technology Development work package led by Dr Michael Short and funded jointly by the BBSRC and EPSRC. They will be part of a large consortium of researchers and industry partners from across the UK.

They will work on existing code developed within the project to deliver, alongside industrial and academic partners, open-source tools and a digitalisation roadmap aimed at accelerating the adoption of digital technologies across the industrial bioenergy sector, including areas such as gasification and anaerobic digestion.

They will develop and apply advanced methods for real-time monitoring, optimisation and control, focusing on improving both sustainability and economic performance. This will involve the use of traditional optimisation techniques as well as machine learning and artificial intelligence approaches. The role requires the ability to use initiative and creativity to identify suitable research methods and techniques, with strong Python programming skills being essential. Familiarity with the research group's existing methods and tools is also required, together with the ability to be regularly present on-site at the University of Surrey.

The successful candidate will form an important part of a multidisciplinary team and will be expected to contribute to project management activities, undertake analysis and interpretation of research results, and support the work of other team members. They may be required to collect and interpret data from a wide range of sources and collaborate with multiple universities and industrial partners. Responsibilities will include writing up research findings and preparing papers for the project team, academic journals, conferences and other dissemination activities. The postholder will be expected to plan and manage their own research programme in collaboration with colleagues and industry partners, present findings and models at workshops, and provide user training where required.

In addition, the role may involve administrative functions associated with the funded project, including organising meetings, maintaining project documentation, and implementing procedures to support accurate and timely reporting and financial management. There may also be opportunities to supervise junior research staff as required.

 About you

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Assistant (RA) wishing to advance their career in a research-driven, interdisciplinary environment, beginning 1 January 2027 at the latest. 

How to apply

To apply, please submit your CV & cover letter via the University website. You will also be asked some brief questions to help us understand your suitability for the position.

This is a fixed term contract for up to 10 months.

If there are any questions associated with the role, please do not hesitate to contact Dr Michael Short (m.short@surrey.ac.uk).

The opportunity
We are seeking an innovative and dedicated Research Fellow to join our research team on MIMETIC, a new AHRC-funded project building a UK foundation model for the creative industries. This is one of two identical 0.5 FTE (full-time equivalent) Research Fellow posts on the project. You will be managed by Professor Mick Grierson and will work alongside the second Research Fellow in Creative Machine Learning, a Post-Doctoral Research Fellow in Human-Computer Interaction supervised by Professor Rebecca Fiebrink, and the wider MIMETIC team of researchers and industry partners.
Your profile

You will hold a PhD (or equivalent experience) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Creative Computing or a related area, with a specific focus on generative models for audio, music, image or video. Candidates in the final year of a PhD, or who do not hold a PhD but have published peer-reviewed work in the field at ACM or comparable international conferences (for example in creativity and computation, computer music, computer vision or machine learning), will be considered. 

 

You will have demonstrable experience of designing, training and evaluating deep generative models, in particular diffusion or related latent generative models, for audio, music, image or video, including experience of training large models on multi-GPU infrastructure. 

 

You will have experience of building and maintaining large multimodal datasets, including data pipelines, annotation, metadata, provenance and licensing, and an understanding of copyright and data protection as they apply to training data. You will also have strong programming skills in Python and experience with machine learning frameworks (for example PyTorch) and with the tooling used for large-scale training, such as distributed training, experiment tracking and large-scale data storage. 

 

A record of research dissemination in the field is essential, for example through publication at ACM or comparable conferences, open-source software releases, or public model releases. 

 

You will have the ability to plan and prioritise your own work and that of others, monitoring progress and taking corrective action where necessary to ensure that it is completed in line with strategic objectives. You will also be able to initiate processes and procedures to resolve problems, anticipating difficulties and identifying practical ways of overcoming or preventing them. 

 

You will contribute to advancing professional practice/research or scholarly activity in your own area of specialism. 

We are UAL

University of the Arts London (UAL) generates and inspires the creativity the world needs for a better future. Since 1842, our colleges have been defining creative education. With curiosity, imagination and intent we make work which creates lasting change for people and our planet. London is core to who we are, a place where we meet and share ideas with people from different backgrounds and cultures.

Our creative network influences learning, culture, industry and society on a global scale. Our academics and practitioners deliver creative education and inspire new ways of thinking through research and innovation. We work with students at every level from pre-degree and short courses to postgraduate and online learning, enabling them to build the careers they want. Together, we are a community of makers, thinkers, pioneers and storytellers redesigning the future.

As a University, we are ranked second in the world for Art and Design. We are formed of 6 Colleges with unique histories and identities: Camberwell College of Arts, Central Saint Martins, Chelsea College of Arts, London College of Communication, London College of Fashion and Wimbledon College of Arts. UAL also has 4 Institutes, 5 Research Centres, 1 Pre-Degree School and 2 subsidiary companies delivering specialist activities.

We are a global University, welcoming over 22,000 students and 6,000 staff from 130 countries. We aim to be a university where people can be themselves and feel supported to reach their full potential. That’s why we are proud to hold a Bronze Award from the Race Equality Charter (REC), are members of the Business Disability Forum and Employers for Carers, and maintain our status as a Disability Confident Scheme and Living Wage employer.

Application process

We operate a fair and open anonymous selection process. Thus, you will need to create an account and submit an application through our application portal. As part of this, you will need to provide a supporting statement/answer some competency questions to demonstrate your suitability. Our recruitment process involves: Application, Shortlisting, Interview and Assessment, Offer, Onboarding.

We understand the benefits of using AI in work. But, if you are thinking of using it to submit an application, we ask you to think about what value it adds. AI tools tend to lack the personal touch and authenticity we value in candidates. We encourage you to showcase your unique knowledge and skills using your own voice.

If we receive a high volume of applications, the closing day date might close early. We aim to communicate any changes to the closing date with at least 24 hours’ notice. If you have any general questions or have accessibility needs, please refer to our Contact us page.

About the Role

 

We invite applications for a Research Fellow (Post Doc) position at Warwick Business School.

 

Successful candidates will join the FutureFinance.AI Research Group at the Gillmore Centre for Financial Technology. The Research Group draws interdisciplinary scholars and thinkers from across the world to redefine and innovate the financial and property technology landscape. The focus of the research group is on the use of AI, machine learning, and data science in the emerging fintech and proptech sectors.  

 

About You

 

We invite applicants with research interests at the intersection of AI and Finance, and an ability to publish in top tier business and interdisciplinary journals. Applicants should hold (or be about to complete) a PhD in Business, Finance, Computer Science, Financial Engineering, FinTech, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Economics, or a related discipline.

 

Strong quantitative and programming skills, fluency in English, and excellent communication and presentation skills are essential. Candidates with expertise in reinforcement learning and/or generative AI are particularly welcome to apply.

 

If you would like to discuss the position, please do feel free to contact Dr Ram Gopal (ram.gopal@wbs.ac.uk).

 

About the Department

 

The primary mission of the Gilmore Centre is to conduct world-class, cutting-edge research at the intersection of finance and technology. The Centre engages in research exploring the transformative impact of emerging technologies like AI, ML, blockchain, mobile payments, cryptocurrencies and crowdfunding platforms on financial activities. 

 

The broad research directions of interest are the following:

 

Societal Impacts and Policy: crypto-currencies, cyber security, financial and privacy regulation, inequality and underserved markets.
Firm and Industry Analysis: blockchain and financial intermediation, smart contracts, nature and source of competition in the financial sector, emerging industry structure, impact of social media on financial markets.
Consumer Analysis: Innovative technology-infused products and services, financial literacy and empowering consumers.
Technology Management: financial principles and instruments to manage data and technology resources such as bandwidth and cloud computing.

 

The FutureFinance.AI Research Group is based in the Gillmore Centre for Financial Technology, whose primary mission is to conduct world-class, cutting-edge research at the intersection of finance and technology. The Gillmore Centre for Financial Technology organizes several academic and industry conferences, workshops, and seminars throughout the year. Successful applicants will be able to join these activities and engage with leading researchers at the Centre. 

 

Warwick Business School (WBS) is a place where big ideas meet real impact. We’re part of a world-class university, but we’re more than just our reputation. For nearly 60 years, we’ve been helping people turn ambition into action, equipping them to make a real difference in the world. 

 

Click here to see our online brochure. This was specifically created for candidates to gain further insight into working at Warwick Business School.

 

We were the first UK business school to achieve triple accreditation (EQUIS, AMBA, AACSB), and our programmes consistently rank among the best - view all of our rankings here. 

 

But what really sets us apart is how it feels to be here. We’re down to earth, collaborative, and proud to create a place where staff, students and alumni feel at home. We want your time here to be as inspiring as it is rewarding, with the support, trust, and opportunities you need to grow both professionally and personally. 

 

 

 

How to Apply

 

To apply, please click APPLY below and submit an application form by the closing deadline.

 

You will be asked to add your personal details and include two attachments:

 

CV
Cover Letter
 

These attachments should:

 

Outline employment and education history (including your most recent employment).
Demonstrate your skills, experience, and qualifications, and how you meet the essential and desirable criteria in the Job Description (attached below).
 

Please ensure your application clearly evidences the essential criteria, as the hiring panel may not be able to shortlist your application if these are not demonstrated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage candidates to submit an application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications.

 

Interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

 

Job Description

 

For more information about essential and desirable knowledge, skills, experience, and qualifications for this position, please refer to the Job Description (JD) by clicking the link below:

 

↪ JD - Research Fellow (621)

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5.

Research Associate in Mathematical and Computational Foundations of Reservoir Computing
Edinburgh, Midlothian, United Kingdom

Role: 
Research Associate in Mathematical and Computational Foundations of Reservoir Computing

Grade and Salary:
 Grade 7 - £38,448 to £46,970 per annum

FTE and working pattern:
 1 FTE (full-time – 35 hours per week) fixed term for 24 months

Holiday Entitlement:
 

33 days annual leave plus 9 buildings-closed days (and Christmas Eve when it falls on a weekday). Use our total rewards calculator: 

 

https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm

 

to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University

 

Purpose of Role

We are recruiting a 24-month, full-time research associate to contribute to the UKRI-funded project “Taking Material Reservoir Computers FARR: Foundations for Adaptation, Resilience and Recovery.” 

Our vision is to develop theoretical and computational foundations for a new generation of adaptable, resilient, and recoverable computing systems. The project brings together researchers from Heriot-Watt, Oxford, Liverpool, Sussex, and Ulster universities to investigate reservoir computing, with a particular focus on its potential for low-power, real-time decision making in challenging environments.

You will undertake original research at the intersection of applied mathematics, statistics, and optimisation to better understand how reservoir computers process and retain information. Your research will focus on characterising the behaviour of reservoir computers, investigating the role of memory in decision-making, and developing methods to quantify uncertainty. You will also develop and evaluate computational approaches that enable reservoir computers to adapt to changing conditions and recover from disruption. 

The successful candidate will be based in the School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences at Heriot-Watt University. You will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of researchers across the five partner institutions.

This work is being undertaken in cooperation with UK Government stakeholders. The successful candidate will be required to obtain security clearance before taking up the post, and must be eligible for UK security clearance in principle, e.g., by nationality (British Citizen) or 5+ years UK residency etc. Eligibility criteria and further information on the process can be found on the UK Government security vetting website, see 

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels.

 

Anticipated start date: January 2027, or a later date by mutual agreement.

 

Candidates can make informal enquiries about this position to Eric Hall 

E.Hall@hw.ac.uk

 OR Michael Lones 

M.Lones@hw.ac.uk

.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

Conduct and disseminate original research aligned with the project, in collaboration with the wider team.

Develop mathematical and statistical methods to characterise reservoir computing systems, with a particular focus on memory, decision-making, and uncertainty quantification.

Develop, implement, and evaluate computational methods to investigate the adaptation, resilience, and recovery of reservoir computing systems.

Work closely with the supervisory team to develop and plan research objectives. 

Prepare research reports and contribute to publications in peer-reviewed journals and conference proceedings.

Present research findings and contribute to technical workshops, seminars, and conferences, as appropriate. 

Undertake training and professional development activities, as necessary and agreed with the supervisory team, to support project objectives and further career development.

Undertake any other duties commensurate with the grade of the post.

Essential & Desirable Criteria

Essential

PhD in mathematical sciences, computer science, or a closely related discipline, or currently working towards the completion of such a PhD.

Experience of mathematical modelling, statistical analysis, or optimisation.

Experience in scientific programming and computational research, using languages such as Python, MATLAB, or Julia.

Experience of, or willingness to work with, researchers from other disciplines.

Evidence of self-motivation and the ability to work independently.

Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Excellent time management and organisational skills, including the ability to prioritise workload.

Desirable

Experience in stochastic processes, dynamical systems, or time-series analysis. 

Experience or knowledge of uncertainty quantification, statistical inference, or information-theoretic methods.

Experience or knowledge of reservoir computing, recurrent neural networks, or nature-inspired computing approaches.

Experience or knowledge of applying multi-objective optimisation algorithms or computational simulation. 

Experience of working in interdisciplinary research teams or industrial collaborative projects.

Evidence of research publications or presentations at academic conferences.

Applications can be submitted up to 11:55pm (UK time) on Thursday 3
rd

Your application should be an authentic representation of your skills, experience and achievements. Applications that appear to have been fully generated by AI may not accurately reflect your suitability for the role and are therefore discouraged.

At interview, candidates will be expected to discuss and provide evidence of the experience, skills and examples included in their application.

We welcome and will consider flexible working patterns e.g., part-time working and job share options.

Heriot-Watt University is committed to securing equality of opportunity in employment and to the creation of an environment in which individuals are selected, trained, promoted, appraised, and otherwise treated on the sole basis of their relevant merits and abilities.  Equality and diversity are all about maximising potential and creating a culture of inclusion for all.

About the Team

You will join an interdisciplinary team working on the UKRI-funded project “Taking Material Reservoir Computers FARR: Foundations for Adaptation, Resilience and Recovery.” This project brings together researchers from Heriot-Watt, Oxford, Liverpool, Sussex, and Ulster universities with expertise spanning mathematics, computer science, robotics, neuroscience, psychology, and materials engineering. The successful candidate will work closely with researchers in mathematics and computer science at Heriot-Watt, while collaborating with colleagues across the wider project consortium. 

You will be based in the School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences at Heriot-Watt University, which comprises the Departments of Mathematics, Computer Science, and Actuarial Mathematics & Statistics. The School has a strong research culture and provides a supportive environment for research collaboration and career development. The School is also home to the Mathematics-Driven Innovate Centre (M-DICE), which provides opportunities to engage with industry and external partners through collaborative research, innovation, and knowledge exchange. 

The Department of Mathematics is part of the Maxwell Institute for Mathematical Sciences, a joint research institute bringing together the mathematical research activities at Heriot-Watt University and at the University of Edinburgh. 

The Department is also a co-founder of the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences (ICMS), which organises international workshops and conferences, attracting leading researchers from around world. Together, these institutions contribute to a vibrant and internationally connected mathematical research community in Edinburgh.

The School of Mathematical and Computer Sciences has an Athena SWAN Silver Award  (see

Our flourishing community will give you the freedom to challenge and to bring your enterprising mind and to help our partners with solutions that can be applied now and in the future. The role

Applications are invited for the role of Postdoctoral Researcher at the Centre for Device Thermography and Reliability (CDTR), led by Professor Martin Kuball.

This role focuses on transforming thermal management/reliability of novel electronic semiconductor devices/chips (including AI chips), using wide and ultra-wide bandgap materials, such as GaN, Ga2O3, BN, AlN and diamond. You will research novel ways of determining device temperature and thermal conductivity and will develop/implement novel heat sinking approaches; this includes the integration of diamond for heat sinking into electronics, microfluidics and the recycling of heat waste energy. You will also assess overall heat transport within the chips, their packaging and systems and use new optical laser-based systems to study temperature and electric fields with sub-micron spatial resolution; as these limit device performance and reliability. You will have the opportunity to study unique device structures and apply new thermal imaging techniques for nm-scale devices. You will aso have access to the extensive device testing suite available in Bristol (from advanced electrical, thermal to electric field analysis), simulation tools (ATLAS, ANSYS), diamond CVD system, laser micromachining, and state-of-the-art clean room. You will collaborate within our 35-member team, our academic and industrial partners and have the opportunity to make a major impact on future power device technology.

The CDTR leads numerous UK and international strategic programmes on power and RF electronics, including European Innovation Accelerator (part of Horizon Europe) programme CoolbrAIn, EPSRC programme grant ULTRAlGaN and the UKRI-funded Innovation and Knowledge Centre REWIRE. This position benefits from the Chair in Emerging Technologies awarded to Professor Kuball by the Royal Academy of Engineering (RAEng) in 2020, and various US funded programmes. 

What will you be doing?

You will advance wide and ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor materials device/AI technology and their understanding.

Responsibilities include: to design, build and use optical laser-based systems for device temperature and material thermal characterization; to develop and implement new heat extraction/spreading solutions; to develop material/device thermal models for device design and to complement experiments.

You will also contribute to managing our thermal characterization laboratory, advise junior group members and support short-term industrial contract.

Postgraduate (PhD) in Physics, Materials Science or Engineering, or be working towards one, or equivalent professional qualification/experience.
Ideally, a good publication record.
Prior experience in semiconductor materials/devices and optical laser-based systems is essential.
Desirable experience in finite element thermal and thermomechanical simulations.
A willingness to work together with, and co-supervise, PhD students.

About the role

Are you a molecular scientist ready to help tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as a Fleming Initiative Research Associate?

Join Dr Jesus Rodriguez-Manzano’s group at Imperial’s Centre for Antimicrobial Optimisation (CAMO) to develop and validate sample preparation and molecular diagnostic methods, and to generate high-throughput PCR and amplicon sequencing data from a large, longitudinal, multi-site study. Your work will produce the curated datasets that underpin environmental and epidemiological modelling across the Fleming Initiative, a partnership between Imperial College London, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and GSK.

What you would be doing

You will play a central role in a multi-site, longitudinal study of how AMR emerges and spreads across clinical and environmental settings, with a focus on extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. As part of the work package responsible for method development, sampling and data generation, you will:

Carry out day-to-day laboratory work, including preparing and extracting environmental samples (water, wastewater, sediment, biosolids and air), optimising assays, and running high-throughput PCR, culture enrichment, library preparation and amplicon sequencing.
Help standardise sampling, processing and analytical methods, including drafting and maintaining standard operating procedures, quality controls, and sample tracking and biobanking records.
Carry out preliminary analysis of PCR and sequencing data, including run quality control, target calling and summary outputs, and prepare curated datasets and metadata for onward analysis.
Work closely with the bioinformatics and modelling teams to ensure smooth data transfer, accurate metadata and alignment across teams and study sites.
Help coordinate project logistics, including reagent management, experiment scheduling and clear, shared documentation.
Contribute figures, methods and results to conference abstracts, reports and peer-reviewed publications.
Support the Fleming Initiative’s vision of putting the public at the heart of its activities by contributing to public engagement and involvement activities.

What we are looking for

You will hold a PhD, or be close to completing one, in microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences or a closely related discipline. You will have hands-on research experience in a broad range of molecular biology techniques, including assay design and optimisation, sample preparation, quantitative PCR (high-throughput, microfluidic or digital) and next-generation sequencing workflows such as library preparation and amplicon sequencing. You will also be comfortable with quality control and preliminary analysis of PCR or sequencing data, statistical methods, and scientific writing for reports and publications. Experience of public engagement is also sought.

Just as important are your skills and attitude. You are a creative problem-solver who can review the literature, develop new ideas, and manage your own work and deadlines with minimal supervision. You communicate clearly, in writing and in person, including about the societal impact of your research. You work well in a team, stay flexible, respect confidentiality, and have strong computer skills. You should be willing to travel in the UK and abroad, and to work occasional out-of-hours or weekends if the project requires it.

What we can offer you

The chance to be part of the Fleming Initiative, a new partnership led by Imperial College London, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and GSK, tackling antimicrobial resistance through a people-centred and convergence science approach.
The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression.
As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes).
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

Further information

Dr Rodriguez-Manzano’s group is at the forefront of developing and applying novel approaches to infectious disease diagnosis, from point-of-care molecular devices to machine-learning-enabled PCR multiplexing, with a particular interest in low-resource settings. The group is based at CAMO within the Department of Infectious Disease, Faculty of Medicine, with state-of-the-art laboratories including a data, molecular and mass spectrometry suite, microbiology laboratories and sensor fabrication facilities. This post is responsible to Dr Jesus Rodriguez-Manzano.

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week).

This role is for a fixed-term contract for 18 months (11 January 2027 – 10 July 2028).

 

*Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum.

postings.advert_text:
Marie Sklodowska-Curie Dual Doctoral Network PhD Fellow in Pedestrian Behaviour Modelling

Are you fascinated by human behaviour? Do you have a strong skillset in mathematical modelling and/or machine learning? Do you want to contribute to making cities better and safer for pedestrians?

STEP-UP (www.project-stepup.eu) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network, training a cohort of researchers to develop better ways of integrating pedestrian needs into transport research, planning and design. 

The network is now recruiting ten doctoral candidates (DCs), who will contribute with complementary perspectives to a shared research agenda and collaborative research community in which they exchange knowledge, learn from one another, and develop a holistic understanding of pedestrian behaviour in urban public spaces. Each PhD position is jointly offered by two academic institutions: a host and a co-host university. 

This double degree arrangement enables each DC to benefit from the complementary expertise of both institutions. DCs will be enrolled in the doctoral programmes of both universities, spend a predefined period at the co-host institution, and will receive a PhD degree from each university upon successful completion of the programme.

In this specific doctoral project, a collaboration between the University of Leeds and the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), the focus is on computational modelling of pedestrian behaviour, and how walking behaviour is affected by secondary task distractions such as mobile phone use. The goal is to develop a simulation model of walking in urban environments, which accurately captures pedestrian walking with and without distractions. The developed model will have important applications in road safety, vehicle automation, and more. 

You will join the vibrant, highly cross-disciplinary Human Factors & Safety research group in Leeds, with members from over 20 countries. Your lead supervisor will be Prof. Gustav Markkula, who will support you in building on his team’s cutting edge modelling research, combining mechanistic, theory-driven modelling with machine learning methods such as reinforcement learning (example paper). You will be able to collect human data, from naturalistic walking and/or using the world-unique VR facilities at Virtuocity. You will spend one year of your PhD at NTUA with co-supervisor Prof. Ioanna Spyropoulou, where you will be able to investigate how your models can be scaled to guide design of safer pedestrian infrastructure. You will also benefit from secondments to other academic and industry partners within STEP-UP.

Eligibility: To meet the requirements of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Dual Doctoral Network, you must:

Not have a previous PhD degree. 
Be eligible to enrol in studies for a doctoral degree (PhD) at the University of Leeds. See eligibility requirements here.
Be eligible to enrol in studies for a doctoral degree also at the National Technical University of Athens. See eligibility requirements here.
You must not have lived or worked in the UK for more than 12 months in the 3 years prior to recruitment date. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account.
There are no restrictions on nationality, but to engage in paid employment you must have the necessary Right to Work in the UK. This may involve obtaining an appropriate visa and the University of Leeds will be able to offer support and advice to the successful candidate.

Please refer to the ‘How to Apply’ section of the Candidate Brief for details of the documentation required as part of your online application.

To explore the post further or for any queries you may have, please contact: 

Prof. Gustav Markkula, Chair in Applied Behaviour Modelling

Tel: +44 (0)113 343 39832 or email: G.Markkula@leeds.ac.uk

 Are you qualified in Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline with a good understanding of applying technology to support business? If so, we want to talk to you about an exciting new Digital Transformation project.

 The University of Liverpool, in collaboration with Clan Contracting Ltd ( www.clan.co.uk/ ), is seeking to recruit a high-calibre graduate with a minimum, upper-second class honours degree (or equivalent) in Engineering, Computer Science or a related technical discipline and a higher degree in a business-related subject to work on a Knowledge Transfer Project (KTP) ( https://iuk-ktp.org.uk ). The KTP is concerned with digitally transforming Clan’s operations. The successful applicant should be able to demonstrate good business process re-engineering skills and ERP adoption and implementation experience compatible with the specific requirements of the programme of work. In addition to a background in digital systems and transformation, candidates should also be able to demonstrate sound commercial awareness.  We are particularly interested in applicants with experience of digital solution design in construction environments and are comfortable working in a dynamic and aspirational business environment. Strong problem-solving abilities in business processes and digital systems are also anticipated.

 The “KTP Associate” will take a leading role in the implementation and delivery of the Knowledge Transfer Project at Clan Contracting. This will require the candidate to demonstrate strong organisational and project management skills, be a self-motivated, self-starter, able to pick up and run with a new project from start to finish and engage with the Clan Contracting team and obtain ‘buy in’ to the project. The post also comes with training, equipment, and travel and subsistence budgets. The KTP Associate will be based at Clan Contracting as an employee of the University of Liverpool. The Associate will have a Clan Contracting supervisory team and a University supervisory team based within the Operations and Supply Chain Management and Civil and Environmental Engineering Departments at the University. Project management will be the responsibility of the Associate with regular meetings with the supervisory team and support from Clan Contracting and the University. The post is initially for three years with a three-month probationary period, but with potential for a permanent position with the company.

 Informal enquiries to Professor Andrew Lyons, Head of Operations and Supply Chain Management.  a.c.lyons@liverpool.ac.uk .

The successful candidate will have a broad competence in any two centuries of early modern (sixteenth to eighteenth century) French literature. The Fellowship is intended for early-career colleagues with less than two years’ full-time postdoctoral research experience by the start date; further information about eligibility is below.

 The role 

 We are seeking a motivated, talented and committed individual to join our team as a Research Technician. This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of a novel haematopoietic stem cell (HSC)-based gene therapy for ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), a rare genetic disorder associated with progressive neurodegeneration.

 You will join the Kemp Lab, based within the School of Psychology and Neuroscience. Our team is dedicated to developing next-generation stem cell and gene therapies for people with neurodegenerative diseases, bringing together expertise in stem cell biology, genetic engineering, and neuroscience.

 Working as part of our collaborative and multidisciplinary research team, you will contribute to cutting-edge translational research using advanced induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-based models and blood samples from UK patients with A-T to develop and evaluate our gene therapy approach. This will involve maintaining iPSC cultures in accordance with relevant International Society for Stem Cell Research (ISSCR) guidelines, generating and characterising HSCs and microglia from iPSCs, and applying molecular and cellular techniques to assess gene therapy efficacy and safety. The project aims to investigate whether correcting HSCs can improve neuroimmune function and provide a potential therapeutic strategy for the neurological complications of A-T.

 What will you be doing? 

 You will contribute to experimental design, data generation and analysis, and the day-to-day running of the laboratory, ensuring compliance with relevant health and safety requirements and institutional policies. Over the two years you will:

 Maintain multiple iPSC lines in accordance with relevant ISSCR guidelines ensuring culture quality, pluripotency and appropriate documentation.

 Differentiate iPSC lines into HSCs and microglia using established protocols, and characterise the resulting cell populations using appropriate molecular and cellular techniques

 Perform functional assays to assess microglial phagocytosis, dynamics, morphology and interactions with neurons , using techniques including spinning-disk confocal microscopy.

 Prepare reagents, maintain stocks of laboratory materials and consumables. You will source and maintain stocks of laboratory materials and consumables.

 Work to ensure a safe working environment. You will ensure compliance with Health and Safety regulations and local policies.

 Training others in processes and procedures. You will interact with and provide guidance, support and training to students conducting research studies or projects.

 You should apply if 

 You are or have the following: 

 Enthusiastic about contributing to the development of novel stem cell and gene therapies for people with neurodegenerative disorders.

 Practical experience working with induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), including their culture, maintenance and differentiation, or related IPSC techniques.

 Experience in molecular biology techniques, such as nucleic acid and protein extraction, PCR, western blotting and ELISA.

 Experience in cell imaging and histological techniques, including immunofluorescence staining and microscopy.

 Excellent IT, organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise multiple tasks, work independently and meet deadlines.

 Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team and communicate effectively.

 Additional information 

 Contract type: Open-ended with funding until 31/12/2028 

 School/Unit: School of Psychology and Neuroscience 

 This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Tuesday 1st December 2026 

 Interviews will be held week commencing 14th December 2026 

 For informal queries please contact: Dr Kevin Kemp, Associate Professor ( kevin.kemp@bristol.ac.uk )

The Centre for High Frequency Engineering (CHFE), within the School of Engineering at Cardiff University, in partnership with IQE, is seeking to recruit a highly motivated researcher to contribute to an exciting, collaborative research and development programme in high-frequency electronics.

The role will involve conducting research to develop high-performance devices for next-generation communications and sensing applications using GaN RF technology platforms. This role offers the opportunity to work within a dynamic, collaborative research environment at Cardiff University, with strong links to industry. Research Fellow

 Coventry University Group – Centre for Future Transport and Cities (CFTC) 

 Competitive starting salary range from £38,784 up to £42, 254 per annum (dependent upon experience) with the potential to progress. A discretionary range for candidates with exceptional experience can be discussed/considered. 

 Our Mission 

 Coventry University is a global Education Group that empowers students and communities to transform their lives and society through teaching, learning, research, and enterprise.

 An ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally.

 Coventry University's Centre for Future Transport and Cities ( CFTC ) is a multidisciplinary research centre developing safer, cleaner, smarter, and more accessible transport and urban-mobility solutions. It brings together expertise in connected and autonomous vehicles, transport safety, sustainable mobility, intelligent infrastructure, and future cities, working with academic, industry, and government partners to translate research into practical applications.

 Access to advanced testing infrastructure is enabled through the Centre for Connected and Autonomous Automotive Research ( CCAAR ), a collaboration between Coventry University and HORIBA MIRA based at MIRA Technology Park. Through CCAAR, CFTC researchers can develop and validate automated-vehicle technologies using facilities including the Assured CAV Highway and two StreetDrone automated-vehicle platforms.

 The Role 

 As Research Fellow within the Centre for Future Transport and Cities you will undertake and play a lead role in the development of impactful research and consultancy activity. Developing and identifying new research objectives, proposals, and impact activities for your own or joint research, while contributing to REF impact rated nationally/internationally excellent.

 You will apply innovative research methods and extend the research portfolio including the publication of your research results and outcomes. Building internal and external networks for the exchange of information and future collaboration, sharing information, and identifying potential sources of funds will play a key part of this role.

 Contributing to teaching, learning and development programmes as appropriate, you will use research findings to inform curriculum development while assisting in the development of student research skills.

 You will specifically be responsible for:

 Defining test scenarios and the Operational Design Domain (ODD) for the 5D RAPID demonstrator in collaboration with project partners.

 Conducting simulations using IPG CarMaker or CARLA and performing vehicle-in-the-loop tests at MIRA's Assured CAV Highway facility to define, measure, and evaluate relevant project KPIs.

 Generating curated datasets, scenario libraries, and workflows to correlate simulation results with proving-ground tests using StreetDrone automated-vehicle platforms and MIRA's Assured CAV Highway facility.

 Conducting a comprehensive Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) to identify cybersecurity threats arising from the integration of Oxford RF 270 radar sensors into the reference vehicle architecture, assess their potential impact, and derive cybersecurity requirements aligned with emerging BSI and ISO guidance on safety and cybersecurity.

 The role will allow you to contribute to the 5D RAPID (5D RADAR PERCEPTION FOR INTELLIGENT DRIVING) project that aims to validate an advanced, high-resolution, multi-focal ADS sensing architecture for fast, accurate, and reliable measurement of dynamic objects, thereby addressing critical corner cases in current autonomous driving systems.

 Qualifications Required 

 PhD (or equivalent) or professional experience equivalent to a PhD demonstrating an ability to carry-out independent research with a 1st Class/2.1 Degree in Computer Science , Cyber Security or Electrical Engineering , or equivalent.

 Our Successful Candidate 

 A highly motivated and experienced Research Fellow with demonstrable expert knowledge and understanding of  Automotive Cyber Security , including experience contributing to the innovation and development of the field. An Advanced knowledge of research methods and techniques with demonstratable adherence to all regulations, you will have the ability to develop research objectives, projects, and proposals for own and joint research.

 Research sufficient to write up research and produce excellent, high-quality publications in high profile peer reviewed journals and present at national/international events, you will be committed to working collaboratively on research development, delivery and dissemination including interdisciplinary or cross-disciplinary research, public engagement, and knowledge exchange.

 Within the Centre, the successful applicant will be expected to lead Coventry University's contribution to the 5D RAPID project, coordinate associated activities, and ensure the timely completion and submission of all planned deliverables. The successful applicant will work closely with Prof. Soufiene Djahel, Dr Hesamaldin Jadidbonab, and Kevin Vincent to achieve the project's technical and strategic objectives.

 For informal enquiries about the position, please contact Prof. Soufiene Djahel at soufiene.djahel@coventry.ac.uk 

 The Benefits 

 As a staff member of Coventry University, you will have access to a wide range of industry leading rewards and benefits which includes:

 Excellent Employers Pension Contribution

 30 days Annual leave plus Bank Holidays

 New Holiday Purchase Scheme up to 5 additional days

 Life Assurance 4x Salary

 BUPA Cash Plan

 50% off Tuition Fees for staff dependants

 CU Reward Scheme

 Discounts across a range of High Street/ Online Retailers

 Cycle To Work scheme

 Our Culture 

 As a global Education Group, equality, diversity, and inclusion are embedded within the fabric of our organisation and are a key focus of our core values. We harness the power and potential of the diverse cultures, backgrounds, abilities, and experiences of our students, colleagues, and partners to create opportunities for all.

Role Description

About the Role

In this fixed-term role, you will develop and validate end-to-end models and simulation tools for resilient timing architectures, addressing key challenges in their reliability and accuracy. You will investigate alternative timing technologies, represented by complementary terrestrial and non-terrestrial sources. The research will quantify timing error budgets and performance under normal, degraded and outage conditions. You will also explore AI and machine learning methods enhancing performance of the integrated timing architectures. These methods will be tested against conventional statistical and model-based approaches. You will validate the results through simulations, experimental trials and experiments using Cranfield’s Time and Frequency Innovation Node and related PNT facilities, in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

About You

You will have a PhD (or be close to completion) in Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics or a related discipline, together with experience in modelling or simulating dynamic, timing or signal-processing systems. You will be comfortable analysing time series data, applying estimation or AI/ML methods, and assessing results quantitatively.

Experience in timing and synchronisation, clock modelling or disciplining, radio navigation, time transfer or alternative timing architectures would be an advantage, as would experience in validating algorithms with laboratory or field data. Familiarity with resilient terrestrial or non-terrestrial timing systems is welcome but not essential.

You will be confident using Python and/or MATLAB for numerical modelling, simulation, data analysis and algorithm development. You will be able to create reproducible tests, evaluate timing quality and performance, and interpret differences between simulated and measured results. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively are important. Experience with time and frequency measurement, C/C++, software-defined radio, instrument control or automated testing would be beneficial.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

Aerospace is at the heart of Cranfield’s global research airport and is renowned throughout the world for its teaching and research in the fields of aviation and aerospace.  Cranfield Aerospace’s six centres are the powerhouses of our world-class research, driving technological and conceptual advances in aeronautics, propulsion engineering, cyber-physical systems and intelligent automation. Through the strong links with industry built over the past 70 years, we focus on defining and delivering the aircraft, airport and airspace management of the future and are the only university in Europe with our own airport and runway. Cranfield Aerospace is internationally recognised as the first choice for research and education in all aspects of aerospace including aircraft, drones, urban air mobility and space.  Find out more about our work here About Aerospace.

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here.

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families. Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here.

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Ivan Petrunin, Professor of Signal Processing and Intelligent Systems, on +44 (0)1234 750111 Ext. 8262 or i.petrunin@cranfield.ac.uk

 Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on E: peoplerecruitment@cranfield.ac.uk. Please quote reference number 5439.

Please note that we reserve the right to close this advert prior to the stated closing date should we receive sufficient numbers of applications. Therefore, we would encourage you to complete and submit your application as soon as possible.

 Location:  Warneford Hospital, Oxford

 The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic.

 The Department of Psychiatry is based on the Warneford Hospital site in Oxford – a friendly, welcoming place of work with an international reputation for excellence. The Department has a substantial research programme, with major funding from Medical Research Council (MRC), Wellcome Trust and National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) and provides highly rated medical training in psychiatry. The Head of Department is Professor Belinda Lennox. 

 We are seeking a medically qualified clinical researcher to support a Wellcome-funded programme investigating the neural and cognitive mechanisms of psychosis. 

 About the Role 

 The post is full-time and funded for 6 months from 1 February 2027. It is based in the Department of Psychiatry at the Warneford Hospital. 

 The clinical assessment and imaging components of this position require regular on-site attendance. Some administrative and analytical work may be undertaken flexibly, by agreement and subject to study delivery. 

 Reporting to Dr Rob McCutcheon, you will join a programme that uses experimental medicine, clinical phenotyping and multimodal neuroimaging to understand abnormalities in brain function and assess the effects of pharmacological interventions.   

 You will support participant recruitment and clinical research visits, including screening, informed consent, clinical and cognitive assessments, research medication procedures where authorised, and multimodal data acquisition. You will work closely with research staff, clinical teams and imaging colleagues, with opportunities to contribute to data analysis, scientific presentations and publications.   

 About You 

 You will hold a medical degree (MBBS or equivalent), full GMC registration with a licence to practise, and have knowledge of Good Clinical Practice. You will also have clinical experience of assessing patients with psychotic disorders or other severe mental illness. 

 You will have excellent organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate complex study visits, maintain accurate records and meet deadlines. You will demonstrate sound clinical judgement and the ability to escalate participant safety concerns promptly. 

 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to build rapport with participants who may be difficult to engage, are essential. 

 Experience of recruiting participants to clinical trials or experimental medicine studies, and experience with neuroimaging and/or neurophysiology (MRI, MEG or EEG), would be desirable.   

 Diversity 

 Committed to equality and valuing diversity, our active Psychiatry People and Culture teams and initiatives including our values and behaviours framework , work to make the Department of Psychiatry as supportive, welcoming and inclusive as possible.   

 Application Process 

 You will be required to upload a covering letter/supporting statement, CV and the details of two referees as part of your online application. Please see the University pages on the application process at https://www.jobs.ox.ac.uk/application-process . 

 The closing date for applications is 12:00 midday on 2 December 2026 .

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

You will have responsibility for the development of processing techniques for nanophotonic devices. This includes developing novel techniques for the site-control of semiconductor quantum dots, grown by MOVPE, and their integration into advanced nanophotonic structures such as QLEDs and site-controlled emitters. Techniques for site-control of quantum dots must have the ability to lead to nano-scale accuracy of quantum dot formation, and must yield quantum dots with near-transform limited linewidths and excellent uniformity in order to be used for the fabrication of quantum optical circuits. You will work within the laboratories of the National Epitaxy facility where extensive MOVPE capability resides and you will be responsible for development of novel semiconductor processing techniques and characterization. You will be responsible for translating these high quality dots into functional nano-photonic devices working with industrial partners.

 

A high degree of innovation is required as the development of novel and pioneering techniques will be required to meet the challenges of scaling this technology as well as excellent planning and coordination skills to work in an industrially lead research programme.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Fabrication of nano-scale photonic structures and the development of novel semiconductor processing techniques to achieve this.
Application of Electron beam lithography and other nanoscale fabrication techniques.
Characterization and analysis of quantum dot materials and associated functional devices. Techniques include photoluminescence spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray analysis, AFM etc.
Contribute fully to regular group meetings, presenting reports of progress internally and to industrial partners.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected.
