About the role

The School of Education and Social Work at the University of Sussex is looking for a Research Fellow to join a multi-disciplinary, multisite team on a new NIHR-funded project: LIMES (Lives behind the numbers, and the numbers of IMpacted livES). The project is a collaboration between Durham University, Kingston University and the University of Sussex and will examine the implementation, effectiveness and economic consequences of Contextual Safeguarding across England as an approach to address extra-familial harm. 

Working with Professor Lisa Holmes you will contribute to the economic evaluation of Contextual Safeguarding. This will involve collecting, managing and analysing quantitative and qualitative data on the activities, staff time and resources associated with implementation, using detailed micro-costing approaches to examine costs and wider economic consequences.

You will contribute to the design and delivery of research activities, support the development of data collection tools and analytical frameworks, and lead specific strands of analysis. You will work closely with local authority partners and the wider research team, contributing to reports, academic publications, presentations and dissemination activities that inform policy and practice for young people affected by extra-familial harm.

About you

You will have a PhD, or be close to completion, in social work, social policy, applied social science, economics, public policy, sociology, psychology or a related discipline. You will have experience of designing and conducting high-quality research and be able to demonstrate strong quantitative and/or mixed-methods analytical skills.

The ability to work independently, take responsibility for delivering agreed outputs and contribute effectively within a collaborative, multi-institutional research team is essential.

Experience of economic evaluation, micro-costing methodologies, administrative data analysis, or applied research in children's social care, safeguarding, youth justice, education, public health or related policy and practice settings would be advantageous. Experience of engaging with practitioners, policy-makers or people with lived experience is also desirable.

You will have excellent organisational, written and verbal communication skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet project deadlines. Above all, you will be committed to producing high-quality research that contributes to improving services and outcomes for children and young people.

About our School

The School of Education and Social Work is divided into two departments:

Department of Education
Department of Social Work and Social Care

In both you’ll find a welcoming and intellectually stimulating environment.

We provide opportunities for learning and professional development in an environment which encourages intellectual engagement, reflection and debate. We offer a range of courses - from first degrees, certificates and diplomas, to Masters level qualifications and PhDs. 

Our teaching is informed by cutting-edge research on issues of significance in education, childhood and youth and social work and social care. Staff across the School are recognised for the quality of their teaching and research locally, nationally and internationally. The School is committed to the highest quality of teaching and has achieved excellent scores in all NSS categories, and faculty members regularly receive University teaching awards and external recognition for their work.

Research undertaken across the school is of immediate policy and practice relevance. We work closely with a wide range of research users and partners, including national governments and international organisations. We actively support the transfer of research insights into practice including through our relationships with local stakeholders and seek to make a real impact on our wider communities. In the 2021 Research Excellence Framework work by the Department for Education was ranked 1st for Research Impact. 

Our four research centres occupy a central place in what is a stimulating, interdisciplinary research environment and together they support and promote the production of rigorous, critically engaged research. Candidates will be invited to join any of the following: 

The Centre for International Education (CIE) – Centre of Excellence
The Centre for Innovation and Research in Childhood and Youth (CIRCY) – Centre of Excellence
The Centre for Social Work Innovation and Research (CSWIR) 
The Centre for Teaching and Learning Research (CTLR)

In the School of Education and Social Work we are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) practices and policies. We want all staff and students to experience our School as a space that enables them to meet their potential and to thrive. We are particularly interested in active work to address inequalities produced around the specific intersections of gender, race, and disability. 

Please find further information regarding the School of Education and Social Work on our website.

The School of Education and Social Work is proud to hold a Bronze Athena Swan Award. 

Why work here

Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme.  

Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. 

Find out more about our reward and benefits package. 

Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion. 

Further Key Information 

Please contact Lisa Holmes L.J.Holmes@sussex.ac.uk for informal enquiries.

The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Role Description
Department

We are seeking a comparative archaeologist with expert knowledge  of either South Asian or Chinese archaeology to join us in the Department of Archaeology at the University of York and assemble and analyse quantitative data on premodern economies. The position will play a key role in the Leverhulme-funded “Premodern Economics, Future Sustainability: Social Metabolism Across Deep Time (PERSIST)” project, which will work across disciplines to bring evidence from past economic systems into debates about future sustainability.  

Envisioning sustainable futures is difficult because we rely overwhelmingly on the experience of modern societies, overlooking the vast diversity of economic systems in the past. PERSIST addresses this gap by systematically comparing how eight well-documented premodern societies used different  materials—their “social metabolisms.” PERSIST will compare social metabolisms to assess the degree to which each society managed resources, limited inequality, and endured over time. Rather than identifying single successes, it will trace variation across cases to reveal how sustainability was achieved in the past, offering new perspectives on how it can be achieved in the future.

Role

Joining the PERSIST team is an exciting opportunity to bring archaeological insights about past economies into conversations about future sustainability. In this role, you will conduct cutting edge research as part of a team developing new quantitative methods of analysing evidence from the past. You will work with the PERSIST team to seek and assemble data from key excavations, then collaborate in the analysis of that data and its synthesis with evidence from other parts of the globe. You will create datasets from archaeological evidence that can help guide debates about future sustainability, lead and contribute as co-author to publications in major international research journals, and organise workshops and conference sessions dedicated to disseminating the project’s findings.

Skills, Experience & Qualification needed
To assemble archaeological data from key sites in South Asia, China and/or Southwest Asia that are conducive to quantitative analysis
PhD in Archaeology or a closely related discipline (e.g. Anthropology)
Expert Knowledge of South Asian or Chinese archaeology
Knowledge of comparative archaeology
Highly developed communication skills to engage effectively with a wide ranging audience, both orally and in writing, using a range of media
Ability to write up research work for publication in high profile journals and engage in public dissemination
Ability to develop research objectives, projects and proposals for own and joint research, with the assistance of a mentor if required
Competency to conduct individual and collaborative research projects
Competency to make presentations at conferences or exhibit work in other appropriate events
Experience of carrying out both independent and collaborative research

You will investigate how the timing and quality of educators’ support influence children’s exploration, planning, persistence and collaboration during block play. Working with children aged 3–5 in early years settings across Greater London, you will coordinate recruitment and fieldwork, collect video observations and play-based assessments, develop behavioural coding, analyse data, and contribute to educator workshops, publications and practitioner resources.

We seek an experienced, scientifically curious and collaborative full-time Research Assistant to join the Crossley laboratory (https://www.cruk.cam.ac.uk/research-groups/crossley-group/) in the internationally renowned Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute, located on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, Cambridge, UK. You will work alongside Dr Mawer, our Senior Scientific Associate, to bring several ongoing projects to publication, as well as helping to start new projects. In the Crossley research group, we study RNA-DNA hybrid molecules called R-loops - how they are dysregulated in human disease, drive genome instability and inflammation, and how these molecules and cellular responses to them can be harnessed for cancer detection and treatment. We use biochemical, imaging and genomics approaches to study molecular mechanisms underlying R-loop biology and their clinical applications.

You will have strong molecular biology skills (cloning, western blotting, lentiviral infection, qPCR, nucleic acid isolation, immunoprecipitations, microscopy, and flow cytometry) and previous experience of mammalian cell culture. In-depth expertise in at least one of genome stability, RNA biology, chromatin biology, innate immunity or cancer biology is required. Experience in next generation sequencing and/or bioinformatics will be advantageous. The successful candidate will also be required to take on other responsibilities, including preparation of reagents, maintenance of lab stocks and assisting with the day-to-day running of the laboratory.

With recent long-term funding awarded, you will be joining the group at a formative time. You will be enthusiastic about being part of a growing group. This position is a staff vacancy at the University of Cambridge that would allow for the post holder to also undertake a postgraduate course at the University, should an offer of a place be made following the relevant competitive process.

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 1 years in the first instance.

Are you passionate about creating more inclusive and accessible cities? Are you interested in understanding how pedestrians interact with emerging technologies? Do you want to contribute to making future transport systems safer and more empowering for pedestrians with mobility challenges?

STEP-UP (www.project-stepup.eu) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network, training a cohort of researchers to develop better ways of integrating pedestrian needs into transport research, planning and design. 

The network is now recruiting ten doctoral candidates (DCs), who will contribute with complementary perspectives to a shared research agenda and collaborative research community in which they exchange knowledge, learn from one another, and develop a holistic understanding of pedestrian behaviour in urban public spaces. Each PhD position is jointly offered by two academic institutions: a host and a co-host university. 

This double degree arrangement enables each DC to benefit from the complementary expertise of both institutions. DCs will be enrolled in the doctoral programmes of both universities, spend a predefined period at the co-host institution, and will receive a PhD degree from each university upon successful completion of the programme.

In this doctoral project, a collaboration between the University of Leeds and Technische Universität Dresden (TUD), you will investigate how pedestrians with mobility challenges interact with emerging mobility technologies, such as (but not limited to) automated vehicles, intelligent pedestrian crossings, and pedestrian navigation and assistance systems, and identify ways to improve safety, accessibility, and independence. 

You will join the vibrant, highly cross-disciplinary Human Factors & Safety research group in Leeds, with members from over 20 countries. Your lead supervisor will be Associate Prof. Dr Yee Mun Lee and your co-supervisor will be Prof. Natasha Merat. You will use a combination of interviews, workshops, observational studies, co-design methods and virtual reality experiments, using the University's unique Virtuocity immersive simulation facilities to develop and evaluate future mobility solutions in a safe and controlled environment. Your PhD will include one year at TUD, hosted by your co-supervisors Prof. Susann Richter and Prof. Tibor Petzoldt, and a shorter secondment working with inclusive mobility experts at Leeds City Council, where your research can directly inform inclusive design principles, accessibility guidelines, and policy recommendations, to help ensure future mobility technologies work for everyone.

The University of Nottingham is looking to appoint a Research Assistant to support the ROSSINI study. The ROSSINI study is the largest surgical trial in the UK. Its aim is to evaluate key surgical interventions to prevent wound (surgical site) infections. Measuring the primary trial outcome, wound infection, will be completed using digital wound monitoring. This is a novel approach where patients take photos and provide information about their wounds in response to text message requests. Understanding the implementation of digital wound monitoring is key to its successful uptake and delivery as this is unique to each NHS Trust and is influenced by many factors including organisational culture and local practices.

You will work with project leads, Professor Judith Tanner and Professor Stephen Timmons in collaboration with Melissa Rochon (Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust), to explore the implementation and adoption of digital surgical wound monitoring. The implementation of digital wound monitoring at hospital sites in England will be explored at a pre- or early-stage implementation and a later post-implementation phase. In both phases, the post holder will remotely interview key stakeholders from each site, including (but not limited to) clinicians, IT staff, managers and patients. ROSSINI presents a unique opportunity to study implementation of the same technology at different sites, all of which will have their own structures and cultures. The precise number of study sites will depend on the timescale for implementation at the various sites, but we intend to sample as diverse a group of hospitals as we can construct.

Data will be analysed using framework analysis; the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Based on what we learn, we will produce implementation guidance which will enable future users of digital wound monitoring to implement this technology quickly and easily.

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research.

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.

The role

We are seeking a talented and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join our thriving research community as a Research Development Fellow. This new position offers an exciting opportunity to build your own research profile while playing a key role in developing high-quality, impactful research within the Surrey School of Law and across the School of Social Sciences. As a Research Development Fellow, you will work at the heart of our research community, bringing together academic expertise, external partnerships and funding opportunities to support the development of ambitious research programmes. You will collaborate with researchers across one or more of Surrey Law School’s research centres and groups helping colleagues secure external funding, generate impactful research and address major legal, policy, societal, environmental and technological challenges.

This role combines academic research with research development and collaboration. You will help identify funding opportunities, support the development of competitive research proposals and contribute intellectually to projects from conception through to delivery. Working closely with academics, doctoral researchers and external partners, you will help create research programmes that deliver meaningful impact for organisations, policymakers and society. A PhD in Law or a closely related discipline, completed (or very close to completion) by the appointment start date.

Strong research and methodological capability appropriate to the candidate’s field, including doctrinal, theoretical, comparative, socio-legal, empirical, qualitative, quantitative or mixed-methods approaches, as relevant.

The research methodologies you can draw on, with examples of how you have used them.

 As a Research Fellow in Laboratory Systems Biology Cancer Research you will lead the delivery of cutting-edge interdisciplinary research project that combines computational systems biology and laboratory science to better treat cancers.

 This project will focus on experimentally developing biomarkers that will enable computational systems biology models to predict response to therapy in the clinic. You will lead the delivery of this 2-year Future Leaders Fellowship-funded project, produce high-quality academic publications, and share your work nationally and internationally at academic conferences. You will be able to shape the project direction, and pursue the most promising results.

Department: Life Sciences

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 31 January 2030

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Wednesday 16 December 2026, 11:59 pm                       

Full time Salary Range: £37,369 - £46,970 per annum

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Fellow to join Dr Cathy Slack’s group in the School of Life Sciences at Warwick University. Funded by the Leverhulme Trust, the project will investigate how biological sex influences ageing using Drosophila as a model system.

 

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to cathy.slack@warwick.ac.uk.

 

About the Group

Our group aims to understand the molecular and cellular mechanisms that drive animal ageing. We use Drosophila to investigate conserved biological pathways that impact lifespan and healthspan. Our research combines genetics, molecular biology and systems-level approaches. Our research environment provides opportunities to work across a range of experimental platforms, contributing to an internationally relevant and rapidly developing area of ageing research.

 

We and the wider University of Warwick environment offer substantial opportunities for professional development including regular opportunities to attend international conferences.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are looking for someone with expertise in Drosophila genetics and physiology, but we also welcome applications from people with experience of other model organisms particularly in ageing research. Applicants should be proficient in general molecular biology techniques and confocal imaging. Applicants should be able to evidence high-quality research outputs in a relevant field.

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£36,320 per annum).

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£37,369 per annum).

About the Department

School of Life Sciences

For further information about the School of Life Sciences please see our website.

 

We believe that collegiality, openness, inclusivity and diversity are essential for an excellent research and teaching environment. Our workplace ethic has enabled us to gain the Athena SWAN Silver award. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all groups with protected characteristics traditionally under-represented in STEM fields. As part of our ongoing commitment to addressing gender equality under the Athena Swan chartermark, we would particularly encourage and welcome applications from female academics.

 

Please note this is an on-campus based role due to the nature of the work, therefore we cannot accommodate any work from home basis.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications. 

 

Applications should include a CV and a covering letter expressing the reasons for your interest in this post.  Within this information you should demonstrate how you meet the requirements of this role by specific reference to each of the essential, and where applicable, desirable criteria detailed in the person specification and should Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

This information will be used in the shortlisting process and without this evidence we may not be able to shortlist your application. Please note that if you do not evidence the essential requirements, we may not be able to shortlist your application.

 

As part of our ongoing commitment to addressing gender equality under the Athena Swan chartermark, we would particularly encourage and welcome applications from female academics.

 

In your application, you can also include any career breaks you may have taken (e.g. parental/caring/long-term sick leave, part-time work, secondments) or any periods where you were unable or restricted to work because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria. 

 

The interviews will be held on TBC

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.

 About the Role 

 The Photochemistry for Materials lab is looking for a Research Assistant to join our research team at the University of Warwick under the supervision of  Dr Hannes Houck . This position is part-funded through the EPSRC Impact Acceleration Account (IAA) and The Royal Society URF. 

As global dependence on synthetic materials is intensifying, waste-accumulation of end-of-life products has become a major concern. Specifically fast-growing photopolymer technologies that transform a liquid formulation into a permanently hardened crosslinked photo-polymer are problematic as the resulting thermosetting materials can no longer be recycled. Current photochemical processes that underpin light-based curing processes, however, are single-use and fail to address the urgently needed closed loop recycling of the resulting photopolymer materials. The overall ambition is to make fundamental step-changes in photopolymerisation technology so to effectively and completely re-use initial formulations in a closed-loop process. 

You will join our team’s efforts to further develop new photochemistry platforms to scalable and industrially relevant applications of photopolymers with embedded circularity.

Applications are invited to join our investigations on two short-term projects. We are looking for a Research Assistant with specific expertise to undertake the following projects:

 Development of degradable and recyclable materials for photo-3D-printing (EPSRC IAA project Jan-Mar 2027)

 Innovative Thermoreversible Photocycloaddition Reactions for Sustainable Materials Design (URF Apr-Jun 2027)

 More project details are available upon request.

 For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description ( link here ).

 About You 

We are looking to recruit a highly motivated researcher with creative ideas and a passion for science, with knowledge, skills and experience in organic photochemistry in a polymer context, light-based 3D printing techniques, and material characterisation of crosslinked polymer networks.

The project involves several challenging research aspects and provides an opportunity to use and share your research skills and experience across team members yet also allows you to train and develop new skills in photochemistry and polymer science.

You should be able to work both independently and with other team members. You are expected to have excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including to present your work to peers and/or potential stakeholders at internal and external meetings. You will have the opportunity to engage with the wider research community and departmental activities, including the Warwick Polymer Group and during outreach events or teaching activities.

You should have a good honours degree in Chemistry and ideally be near completion of a PhD or equivalent in a relevant scientific discipline (e.g. chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or other science).

 Closing Date: Sunday 29 November 2026, 11:59pm (UK)    

 The interviews will be held on a date to be confirmed.

 Full details of the duties and selection criteria for this role can be found in the vacancy advert on the University of Warwick's jobs pages. You will be routed to this when you click on the 'Apply' button.
